{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_017WaBSjpTRtWBbGaJVDntzc","type":"tool_result","content":"=== sources/full_test.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# full_test.sh — scoring entry point. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\nset -eu\n# The version setup_harness.sh installs. run_conformance.sh refuses a different one, so a\n# passing verdict names a specific exam rather than whichever harness was on PATH.\nTOML_TEST_VERSION=\"${TOML_TEST_VERSION:-v2.2.0}\"\nexport TOML_TEST_VERSION\ngo build -o toml-decoder ./cmd/toml-decoder\nDECODER=\"$PWD/toml-decoder\" exec sh sources/run_conformance.sh\n\n=== sources/run_conformance.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# Run the upstream toml-test conformance suite against the built decoder.\n#\n# Imported sources land in sources/ inside the application directory, so this is\n# normally invoked as `sh sources/run_conformance.sh` from that directory.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   DECODER=./toml-decoder sh sources/run_conformance.sh                        # full suite\n#   DECODER=./toml-decoder sh sources/run_conformance.sh -run 'valid/string/*'  # one group\n#   DECODER=./toml-decoder sh sources/run_conformance.sh -json                  # machine-readable\n#\n# Environment:\n#   DECODER    decoder command. Required — this harness is language-neutral and\n#              deliberately has no default implementation language.\n#   TOML_TEST  absolute path to the toml-test binary (default: found on PATH)\n#\n# Exit code follows the harness exit-status standard in prompts/UAT_SETUP_INSTRUCTIONS.md:\n# 0 only when every test passes, 2 when this harness could not run at all, and any other nonzero\n# when it ran and the decoder failed. A precondition of the harness is never charged to the build.\n\nset -u\n\nif [ -z \"${DECODER:-}\" ]; then\n    echo \"error: DECODER is not set; give the command that runs your decoder.\" >&2\n    exit 2\nfi\n\nif [ -n \"${TOML_TEST:-}\" ] && [ -x \"${TOML_TEST}\" ]; then\n    HARNESS=\"${TOML_TEST}\"\nelif command -v toml-test >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    HARNESS=\"$(command -v toml-test)\"\nelse\n    cat >&2 <<'EOF'\nerror: toml-test not found.\n\nInstall the harness once:\n\n    sh sources/setup_harness.sh\n\nor set TOML_TEST to an existing binary:\n\n    TOML_TEST=/path/to/toml-test sh sources/run_conformance.sh\nEOF\n    # 2, not the shell's own 127: an uninstalled harness says nothing about the decoder, and 127\n    # would be read as an ordinary nonzero exit and charged against the build as a product FAIL.\n    exit 2\nfi\n\n# The suite's identity is part of the verdict. Without this, \"the authoritative suite passed\"\n# names no particular suite: whichever toml-test happened to be on PATH decided the run, and a\n# different version on a different machine is a different exam. Recorded always, and enforced\n# when the caller states which version it expects.\nHARNESS_VERSION=\"$(\"${HARNESS}\" version 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 || true)\"\necho \"harness: ${HARNESS} ${HARNESS_VERSION:-(version unknown)}\" >&2\nif [ -n \"${TOML_TEST_VERSION:-}\" ] && [ -n \"${HARNESS_VERSION}\" ]; then\n    case \"${HARNESS_VERSION}\" in\n        *\"${TOML_TEST_VERSION}\"*) ;;\n        *)\n            echo \"error: harness is ${HARNESS_VERSION}, expected ${TOML_TEST_VERSION}.\" >&2\n            echo \"Run: sh sources/setup_harness.sh\" >&2\n            exit 2\n            ;;\n    esac\nfi\n\nNO_COLOR=1 exec \"${HARNESS}\" test -toml 1.0 -decoder \"${DECODER}\" \"$@\"\n\n=== sources/setup_harness.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# One-time installation of the upstream toml-test conformance harness.\n#\n# Requires network access and a Go toolchain of at least 1.22 — the same floor\n# stack/go.md sets for the deliverable. The Go shipped by apt on Debian and\n# Ubuntu is frequently older and will fail; install the official tarball instead:\n#\n#     curl -sL https://go.dev/dl/go1.24.6.linux-amd64.tar.gz -o go.tgz\n#     sudo tar -C /usr/local -xzf go.tgz\n#     export PATH=/usr/local/go/bin:$PATH\n#\n# Usage:\n#   sh sources/setup_harness.sh              # install to $HOME/.local/bin\n#   GOBIN=/usr/local/bin sh sources/setup_harness.sh\n\nset -eu\n\nTOML_TEST_VERSION=v2.2.0\nGOBIN=\"${GOBIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}\"\n\nif ! command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"error: no go toolchain on PATH; see the header of this script\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\necho \"go:      $(go version)\"\necho \"target:  ${GOBIN}/toml-test\"\necho \"version: ${TOML_TEST_VERSION}\"\n\nmkdir -p \"${GOBIN}\"\nGOBIN=\"${GOBIN}\" go install \\\n    \"github.com/toml-lang/toml-test/v2/cmd/toml-test@${TOML_TEST_VERSION}\"\n\necho\n\"${GOBIN}/toml-test\" version\n\ncase \":${PATH}:\" in\n    *\":${GOBIN}:\"*) ;;\n    *) echo\n       echo \"warning: ${GOBIN} is not on PATH. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_012QVzAwSPJ2xJq5UZsYy54t","type":"tool_result","content":"=== go.mod\nmodule github.com/owner/toml-decoder\n\ngo 1.22\n\n=== cmd/toml-decoder/main.go\n// Command toml-decoder reads a TOML document on stdin and writes its\n// tagged-JSON description to stdout. Diagnostics go to stderr and malformed\n// input exits non-zero.\npackage main\n\nimport (\n\t\"encoding/json\"\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"io\"\n\t\"os\"\n\n\t\"github.com/owner/toml-decoder/internal/toml\"\n)\n\nfunc main() {\n\tif err := run(os.Stdin, os.Stdout); err != nil {\n\t\tfmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, \"toml-decoder:\", err)\n\t\tos.Exit(1)\n\t}\n}\n\n// run decodes the document on in and encodes the result as JSON to out.\nfunc run(in io.Reader, out io.Writer) error {\n\tdoc, err := toml.Decode(in)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"decode: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\treturn json.NewEncoder(out).Encode(doc)\n}\n\n=== cmd/toml-decoder/main_test.go\npackage main\n\nimport (\n\t\"bytes\"\n\t\"encoding/json\"\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"os\"\n\t\"os/exec\"\n\t\"path/filepath\"\n\t\"reflect\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\t\"testing\"\n\n\t\"github.com/owner/toml-decoder/internal/toml\"\n)\n\nconst moduleRoot = \"../..\"\n\nfunc TestGoModDeclaresModuleWithoutRequire(t *testing.T) {\n\tdata, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(moduleRoot, \"go.mod\"))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"read go.mod: %v\", err)\n\t}\n\ttext := string(data)\n\tif strings.Contains(text, \"require\") {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"go.mod declares a require directive:\\n%s\", text)\n\t}\n\tif !strings.Contains(text, \"module github.com/owner/toml-decoder\") {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"go.mod does not declare the module path:\\n%s\", text)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestEntryPointIsPackageMain(t *testing.T) {\n\tdata, err := os.ReadFile(\"main.go\")\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"read main.go: %v\", err)\n\t}\n\tif !strings.Contains(string(data), \"package main\") {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"main.go is not a package main\")\n\t}\n\tinfo, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(moduleRoot, \"internal\", \"toml\"))\n\tif err != nil || !info.IsDir() {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"internal/toml is not a directory: %v\", err)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestDecoderCommandBuildsWithStandardLibrary(t *testing.T) {\n\tbin := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), \"toml-decoder\")\n\tcmd := exec.Command(\"go\", \"build\", \"-o\", bin, \"./cmd/toml-decoder\")\n\tcmd.Dir = moduleRoot\n\tif out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01TXPkFzTdfPvwyd1HzfRxm1","type":"tool_result","content":"The \"test\" command runs the test cases.\n\nThe way toml-test works is that for every test case it executes a \"decoder\"\ncommand, which reads TOML from stdin and then outputs JSON describing that TOML\n(or returns an error if it thinks the TOML isn't valid). Encoder tests work the\nsame except in reverse: it reads JSON and transforms that to TOML.\n\nThere are three types of tests:\n\n    valid      Valid TOML that the decoder command should describe as JSON.\n    invalid    Invalid TOML files that should be rejected with an error.\n    encoder    JSON that the encoder command should transform to TOML.\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing a decoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    A decoder reads TOML data from stdin and outputs a JSON description to\n    stdout and exits with code 0. If the TOML data is invalid, it must exit\n    with code 1. It's recommended to write an error message to stderr.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        toml_data = read_stdin()\n\n        parsed_toml = decode_toml(toml_data)\n\n        if error_parsing_toml():\n            print_error_to_stderr()\n            exit(1)\n\n        print_as_json_description(parsed_toml)\n        exit(0)\n\n    Details of the JSON format is explained below in \"JSON description\".\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing an encoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    An encoder is the reverse of a decoder; it reads a JSON description from\n    stdin converts that to TOML.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        json_data = read_stdin()\n\n        json_description = decode_json(json_data)\n\n        print_as_toml(json_description)\n        exit(0)\n\n\u001b[1mJSON description\u001b[0m\n\n    TOML is described with JSON as follows:\n\n    - TOML tables correspond to JSON objects.\n    - TOML arrays correspond to JSON arrays.\n    - TOML values correspond to a JSON object of the form:\n      {\"type\": \"{TOML_TYPE}\", \"value\": \"{TOML_VALUE}\"}\n\n    In the above, TOML_VALUE is always a JSON string (even for integers or\n    bools), and TOML_TYPE may be one of: string, integer, float, bool,\n    datetime, datetime-local, date-local, or time-local.","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"d83bed2b-d12c-4527-a301-298888c1389d","uuid":"79ead345-8147-42d3-ab68-23fb349ec15f","timestamp":"2026-10-14T13:03:52.436Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"The \"test\" command runs the test cases.\n\nThe way toml-test works is that for every test case it executes a \"decoder\"\ncommand, which reads TOML from stdin and then outputs JSON describing that TOML\n(or returns an error if it thinks the TOML isn't valid). Encoder tests work the\nsame except in reverse: it reads JSON and transforms that to TOML.\n\nThere are three types of tests:\n\n    valid      Valid TOML that the decoder command should describe as JSON.\n    invalid    Invalid TOML files that should be rejected with an error.\n    encoder    JSON that the encoder command should transform to TOML.\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing a decoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    A decoder reads TOML data from stdin and outputs a JSON description to\n    stdout and exits with code 0. If the TOML data is invalid, it must exit\n    with code 1. It's recommended to write an error message to stderr.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        toml_data = read_stdin()\n\n        parsed_toml = decode_toml(toml_data)\n\n        if error_parsing_toml():\n            print_error_to_stderr()\n            exit(1)\n\n        print_as_json_description(parsed_toml)\n        exit(0)\n\n    Details of the JSON format is explained below in \"JSON description\".\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing an encoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    An encoder is the reverse of a decoder; it reads a JSON description from\n    stdin converts that to TOML.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        json_data = read_stdin()\n\n        json_description = decode_json(json_data)\n\n        print_as_toml(json_description)\n        exit(0)\n\n\u001b[1mJSON description\u001b[0m\n\n    TOML is described with JSON as follows:\n\n    - TOML tables correspond to JSON objects.\n    - TOML arrays correspond to JSON arrays.\n    - TOML values correspond to a JSON object of the form:\n      {\"type\": \"{TOML_TYPE}\", \"value\": \"{TOML_VALUE}\"}\n\n    In the above, TOML_VALUE is always a JSON string (even for integers or\n    bools), and TOML_TYPE may be one of: string, integer, float, bool,\n    datetime, datetime-local, date-local, or time-local.","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01TXPkFzTdfPvwyd1HzfRxm1","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"stdout %q is not JSON: %v\", stdout, err)\n\t}\n\twant := map[string]map[string]string{\"n\": {\"type\": \"integer\", \"value\": \"1\"}}\n\tif !reflect.DeepEqual(decoded, want) {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"stdout decodes to %v, want %v\", decoded, want)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestBinaryRejectsControlCharacterInComment(t *testing.T) {\n\tbin := buildDecoderBinary(t)\n\terr, stdout := runDecoderBinary(t, bin, \"# \\x01\\nn = 1\\n\")\n\tassertExitNonZero(t, err)\n\tif len(stdout) != 0 {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"stdout = %q, want empty\", stdout)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestBinaryRejectsInvalidUTF8(t *testing.T) {\n\tbin := buildDecoderBinary(t)\n\terr, stdout := runDecoderBinary(t, bin, \"\\xff\")\n\tassertExitNonZero(t, err)\n\tif len(stdout) != 0 {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"stdout = %q, want empty\", stdout)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc assertExitNonZero(t *testing.T, err error) {\n\tt.Helper()\n\texitErr, ok := err.(*exec.ExitError)\n\tif !ok || exitErr.ExitCode() == 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"binary exit = %v, want non-zero exit\", err)\n\t}\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_014NDjXh2cn6hwp3bkeUK9fy","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"go build failed: %v\\n%s\", err, out)\n\t}\n\treturn bin\n}\n\n// runDecoderBinary feeds stdin to bin and returns its stdout and exit error.\nfunc runDecoderBinary(t *testing.T, bin, stdin string) ([]byte, error) {\n\tt.Helper()\n\tcmd := exec.Command(bin)\n\tcmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(stdin)\n\tvar stdout bytes.Buffer\n\tcmd.Stdout = &stdout\n\terr := cmd.Run()\n\treturn stdout.Bytes(), err\n}\n\nfunc TestBinaryDecodesValueBeforeTrailingComment(t *testing.T) {\n\tbin := buildDecoderBinary(t)\n\tstdout, err := runDecoderBinary(t, bin, \"n = 1 # note\\n\")\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"binary exit = %v, want 0\", err)\n\t}\n\tvar decoded map[string]map[string]string\n\tif err := json.Unmarshal(stdout, &decoded); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"stdout %q is not JSON: %v\", stdout, err)\n\t}\n\twant := map[string]map[string]string{\"n\": {\"type\": \"integer\", \"value\": \"1\"}}\n\tif !reflect.DeepEqual(decoded, want) {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"stdout decodes to %v, want %v\", decoded, want)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestBinaryRejectsControlCharacterInComment(t *testing.T) {\n\tbin := buildDecoderBinary(t)\n\tstdout, err := runDecoderBinary(t, bin, \"# \\x01\\nn = 1\\n\")\n\tassertExitNonZero(t, err)\n\tif len(stdout) != 0 {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"stdout = %q, want empty\", stdout)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestBinaryRejectsInvalidUTF8(t *testing.T) {\n\tbin := buildDecoderBinary(t)\n\terr, stdout := runDecoderBinary(t, bin, \"\\xff\")\n\tassertExitNonZero(t, err)\n\tif len(stdout) != 0 {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"stdout = %q, want empty\", stdout)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc assertExitNonZero(t *testing.T, err error) {\n\tt.Helper()\n\texitErr, ok := err.(*exec.ExitError)\n\tif !ok || exitErr.ExitCode() == 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"binary exit = %v, want non-zero exit\", err)\n\t}\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":61,"oldLines":7,"newStart":61,"newLines":7,"lines":[" "," func TestBinaryRejectsInvalidUTF8(t *testing.T) {","   bin := buildDecoderBinary(t)","-  err, stdout := runDecoderBinary(t, bin, \"\\xff\")","+  stdout, err := runDecoderBinary(t, bin, \"\\xff\")","   assertExitNonZero(t, err)","   if len(stdout) != 0 {","     t.Errorf(\"stdout = %q, want empty\", stdout)"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_016aHxA5gR2ybLXdes8W6f1i","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}
